area: Claude Code plugin eval runner (`claude plugin eval` / `claude plugin eval init`) — case format, graders, runs, ablation, thresholds, reports, and availability, as observed 2026-09-02

facts.behavior: "Run eval cases (<eval dir>/**/case.yaml or prompt.md + graders/*.md; the eval dir is evals/ unless --eval-dir or the manifest says otherwise) against a plugin and report scored results." The command scans the eval dir recursively for either a self-contained case.yaml or a folder pair of prompt.md plus a graders/ directory of *.md files.
facts.limits: Only these two layouts are recognized. In this repo's own suite (plugins/house/evals/**, 12 cases) every case uses prompt.md + graders/*.md; no case.yaml file exists anywhere in the tree, so the case.yaml layout was not independently observed in a real file.

facts.feature: Target resolution and automatic baseline arm
facts.behavior: "Target is a path, a plugin name, or a `plugin@marketplace` id — installed and skills-dir plugins both resolve (and add a no-plugin baseline arm)".
facts.limits: The no-plugin baseline arm is only added when the target actually resolves to a real installed or skills-dir plugin; this is the same condition that flips --ablation's default (see ablation fact).

facts.feature: Eval directory default and results path
facts.behavior: "--eval-dir <dir> Directory name (below the plugin) that holds the eval cases; results go to <plugin>/<dir>/results/ — for an installed-plugin target, ./<dir>/results/ with this flag, else ./evals/results/ (default dir: the manifest's experimental.evals value, else evals/)".
facts.limits: The results path shape differs depending on whether the target is an installed plugin vs. a local path target.

facts.behavior: Real case files in this repo carry YAML frontmatter with max_turns, timeout_seconds, allowed_tools (a bracketed tool list), and runs, e.g. plugins/house/evals/branch-and-pr/prompt.md: `max_turns: 20`, `timeout_seconds: 300`, `allowed_tools: [Bash, Write]`, `runs: 3`, followed by the free-text prompt body. Observed max_turns ranged 15-30 and timeout_seconds 300-600 across the 12 cases in this repo.
facts.limits: Only max_turns, timeout_seconds, allowed_tools, and runs were directly observed in real files. A repo secondary source (docs/handbook/sources/testing-sweep.md, a dated 2026-08-24 survey, not independently verified here) additionally lists name, tags, plugins, model, and env as accepted frontmatter keys, with defaults runs:3, max_turns:10, timeout_seconds:300 when a case omits them — this default-value claim was not confirmed against primary CLI output.
facts.citation: plugins/house/evals/branch-and-pr/prompt.md (read directly); default values per docs/handbook/sources/testing-sweep.md, unverified against primary source

facts.behavior: The CLI's own --help phrases case.yaml and "prompt.md + graders/*.md" as two alternative complete case formats ("case.yaml or prompt.md + graders/*.md"). A repo secondary source instead describes case.yaml as an *optional supplementary* file alongside prompt.md + graders/*.md, holding `context.scaffold_script` / `history_file` / `add_dirs` config, i.e. additive rather than an alternative full format.
facts.limits: These two characterizations were not reconciled — no case.yaml file exists anywhere in this repo to confirm either reading, so its exact schema (whether it embeds the prompt text itself, or only scaffold/context config) is unconfirmed.
facts.citation: claude plugin eval --help ("or" framing); docs/handbook/sources/testing-sweep.md (additive framing, unverified secondary source)

facts.behavior: "--scaffold Run each case's scaffold_script (runs author-supplied bash as you; off by default — only use on case files you authored)"; "--no-scaffold Explicitly skip scaffold_script"; "--keep-temp Preserve scaffold dirs for debugging".
facts.limits: scaffold_script never runs unless --scaffold is explicitly passed, and it then executes as the invoking user's own shell — the CLI's own text is an explicit trust warning, not just a feature note.

facts.behavior: Instantiated repeatedly in real grader files, e.g. plugins/house/evals/branch-and-pr/graders/no-local-merge-back-onto-main.md: `type: regex`, `target: trace`, `pattern: git\\s+(merge|rebase)\\b`, `match: not_contains`, `weight: 0.5`. `target` is also seen as `last_message` or `{source: file, path: "repo/package.json"}`; `match` is seen as `contains` or `not_contains`; an optional `flags: i` was seen for case-insensitive matching.
facts.limits: Schema fields confirmed only for target ∈ {trace, last_message, file-source object}, pattern, match, flags, weight — no other match modes were observed.
facts.citation: plugins/house/evals/*/graders/*.md (multiple files read directly, e.g. no-local-merge-back-onto-main.md, no-env-var-bypass-added.md)

facts.behavior: Instantiated repeatedly, e.g. plugins/house/evals/not-evaluable-verdict/graders/verdict-is-not-evaluable.md: `type: llm`, `focus: last_message`, `weight: 1`, followed by a free-text body instructing the judge model with explicit "Score HIGH when..." / "Score LOW when..." criteria. `focus` is also seen as `trace` or a `{source: file, path: ...}` object.
facts.limits: The judge model used to score `llm` graders defaults to Haiku (see judge-model fact) and is described elsewhere as noisy on long inputs (see grader-ladder fact).
facts.citation: plugins/house/evals/not-evaluable-verdict/graders/verdict-is-not-evaluable.md (read directly), and other llm graders in the same tree

facts.feature: Grader types — tool_used, incl. Skill-firing check
facts.behavior: Instantiated e.g. plugins/house/evals/positive-and-negative-control/graders/check-invoked-more-than-once.md: `type: tool_used`, `tool: Bash`, `input_match: check-unique-ids|check:unique-ids`, `min: 2`, `weight: 0.5`; and plugins/house/evals/explicit-model-tier/graders/every-subagent-call-sets-a-model.md uses `tool: Task`, `input_match: model`, `min: 3`. The CLI's own --help confirms `tool_used: Skill` specifically as the mechanism for detecting whether a plugin's skill fired: graders "marked with-only, incl. `tool_used: Skill`, are a plugin-fired indicator rather than part of the score" under ablation.
facts.limits: Confirmed fields: tool, input_match (regex), min, weight; `max` is named in --help/secondary docs but not observed in a real file in this repo.
facts.citation: claude plugin eval --help (tool_used: Skill as ablation indicator); plugins/house/evals/positive-and-negative-control/graders/check-invoked-more-than-once.md (schema fields, read directly)

facts.behavior: Not instantiated in any file in this repo's own eval suite. A repo secondary source lists a total of six grader types — regex, tool_used, tool_order, file_exists ("a glob over created paths"), llm, baseline. The CLI's own --help independently corroborates that `llm` and `baseline` are grouped as "paid graders (llm/baseline)" that get skipped on a cost-ceiling overrun while other (free/deterministic) graders keep scoring.
facts.limits: tool_order and file_exists field-level schemas are not confirmed from any primary source or real file — only their names and one-line descriptions, from a secondary survey document.
facts.citation: claude plugin eval --help ("paid graders (llm/baseline)" phrase, confirming the llm/baseline split); docs/handbook/testing.md and docs/handbook/sources/testing-sweep.md for the full six-type list and tool_order/file_exists names, unverified against a real case file

facts.behavior: Every grader file observed carries a `weight` field (values seen: 1, 0.5, 0.25) alongside its type-specific fields.
facts.limits: No source found (CLI help, docs pages, or repo files) states how per-grader weights combine into a case's overall score (e.g. weighted average vs. weighted sum vs. normalization) — not documented anywhere reachable in this research.
facts.citation: plugins/house/evals/*/graders/*.md (weight field observed across ~25 grader files, e.g. docs-ride-along/graders/readme-explains-what-it-does.md)

facts.behavior: "--runs <n> Override per-case runs (default: case.runs ?? 3)".
facts.limits: The default is the case's own `runs` frontmatter value if set, else 3; every real case in this repo explicitly sets `runs: 3` itself, matching the fallback default.

facts.behavior: "--threshold <0..1> Exit 1 if any case score is below this threshold (default: 1.0)".
facts.limits: The default of 1.0 requires a perfect score on every case to exit 0; the check is per-case ("any case score"), not an aggregate across the suite.

facts.behavior: "--ablation <mode> Run a no-plugin baseline arm and report the score delta (none | with-without; default: with-without whenever a plugin resolves — by name, or from the target path — and none when nothing does; under with-without, graders marked with-only, incl. `tool_used: Skill`, are a plugin-fired indicator rather than part of the score)".
facts.limits: Defaults to none (no baseline arm, no delta) when the target does not resolve to an identifiable plugin; with-only graders are explicitly excluded from the scored total in with-without mode and instead only indicate whether the plugin fired.

facts.behavior: "--max-cost-usd <usd> Optional hard cost ceiling; abort and report partial results if hit (exit 2). Overrun is bounded to one agent run — when that run breaches, paid graders (llm/baseline) are skipped while free graders still score it. Runs are already bounded by max_turns and timeout_seconds — only set this when you need a strict budget".
facts.limits: Unset by default — the only built-in cost bound absent this flag is max_turns/timeout_seconds per case, not a dollar ceiling. On overrun only the paid (llm/baseline) graders are skipped for that run; free graders still run and score it, and results are reported as partial rather than discarded entirely.

facts.behavior: "--mocks <mode> Mock stand-ins for MCP servers, from <eval dir>/mocks/ (record | off; default: record — off spawns the real servers, gated by --allow-tools as usual)".
facts.limits: Scoped specifically to a plugin's declared MCP servers; even with --mocks off, real MCP tool calls (mcp__*) still go through the same --allow-tools gate as any other gated tool.

facts.behavior: "--allow-tools <tools...> Operator grant for gated tools (Bash, Write, Edit, WebFetch, mcp__*). Supports Tool(pattern:*) syntax".
facts.limits: The gated-tool set is fixed and named explicitly: Bash, Write, Edit, WebFetch, and any mcp__* tool. This session could not observe the actual denial behavior for an ungranted gated tool during a live run, since every run/init invocation was blocked by the early-access gate before reaching tool execution.

facts.behavior: Two separate override flags exist: "--model <model> Override model for all cases" (the model the agent-under-test runs as) and "--judge-model <model> Override LLM-grader model (default: haiku)" (the model scoring `llm`-type graders).
facts.limits: --model applies uniformly across every case in a run — no per-case model override flag is documented. The judge-model default of haiku is the cheapest tier, consistent with cost-conscious grading.

facts.feature: Case filtering by glob and tag
facts.behavior: "--case <glob> Filter cases by name glob" and "--tag <tag...> Filter cases by tag (repeatable)".
facts.limits: Tag filtering requires cases to declare a `tags` field in frontmatter; this field was not observed in any real case file in this repo (all use max_turns/timeout_seconds/allowed_tools/runs only), so it is unconfirmed as actually populated in practice here, only documented as an accepted key by a secondary source.
facts.citation: claude plugin eval --help (flags); docs/handbook/sources/testing-sweep.md (tags frontmatter key, unverified)

facts.behavior: "--json [path] Print the full run result (prompts, graders, per-run scores) as JSON to stdout, or write it to this .json file".
facts.limits: Distinct from the always-written aggregate-result.json in the results dir (see output-dir fact) — this flag is for a fuller, opt-in dump including prompts and grader definitions, not just scores.

facts.behavior: "--report <path> Write the self-contained HTML report (scores, prompts, grader verdicts) to <path> instead of the results dir"; "--no-publish Keep the HTML report local only; skip publishing it to claude.ai"; "--publish-report Also require publishing the report to claude.ai (already the default when your account supports it); explains why if unavailable".
facts.limits: Publishing to claude.ai is the default only when the invoking account supports it; when it doesn't, the CLI states why rather than silently skipping or failing.

facts.behavior: "--output-dir <dir> Directory for aggregate-result.json (default: ./<eval dir>/results/<timestamp>/)".
facts.limits: Timestamped subdirectory per run by default, so successive runs don't overwrite each other's results.

facts.behavior: "--verbose Log per-message trace events to the debug log (use --debug-file to read them)".
facts.limits: Writes to the general debug log, not a dedicated eval log file; requires the separate --debug-file mechanism to read.

facts.behavior: "claude plugin eval init [options] [name] — Author an eval suite under the eval dir (evals/ unless --eval-dir or the manifest says otherwise) via an interview that sources inputs and designs graders. Use --bare <name> for a blank single-case template." Options: `--bare` ("Write a blank template (prompt.md + graders/criteria.md) instead of running the interview"), `--eval-dir <dir>`, `-i, --interactive` ("Run the authoring interview (already the default in a terminal); requires an interactive terminal").
facts.limits: The full interview mode requires an interactive terminal; this session's own non-interactive attempt to run `claude plugin eval init demo-case --bare` was intercepted by the early-access gate before the interactive-terminal requirement could be independently exercised, so its exact non-interactive failure message (absent gating) is not directly observed here.

facts.feature: Availability: early-access gate blocks every real invocation
facts.behavior: Live in this session: `claude plugin eval` (bare) and `claude plugin eval init demo-case --bare` both printed only "`plugin eval` is currently in early access" and exited with code 1 — no files were written, no interview ran, no cases executed. `claude plugin eval --help` and `claude plugin eval init --help`, run in the same session, printed their full usage text with no gating message.
facts.limits: The gate applies to every actual action (run, init/interview, init --bare) but not to --help text itself. This session's account/session specifically does not have the feature enabled — it is described (by the tool's own listing) as "early access" and gated at an organizational rollout level, not a global unavailability.
facts.citation: claude plugin eval and claude plugin eval init demo-case --bare (both run live in this session; exit code 1)

facts.behavior: "Code-based graders" are "fast, cheap, objective, reproducible" but brittle to valid variations (string matching, binary tests, static analysis, outcome verification). "Model-based graders" are flexible for open-ended tasks but "non-deterministic, more expensive than code, requires calibration with human graders." "Human graders" provide "gold standard quality" but are expensive/slow, best reserved for calibration.
facts.limits: This is general Anthropic engineering guidance for building agent evals broadly, not documentation of `claude plugin eval` specifically — the plugin eval runner's own regex/tool_used/llm/baseline split (see grader-type facts) maps onto this three-class framing but isn't stated as being derived from it.

facts.feature: Anthropic guidance: pass@k vs pass^k, task count, isolation, balance
facts.behavior: pass@k measures "the likelihood that an agent gets at least one correct solution in k attempts"; pass^k measures "the probability that all k trials succeed," called out as critical for customer-facing agents. "20-50 simple tasks drawn from real failures is a great start." Each trial should start from a clean/isolated environment to avoid shared-state correlated failures. "Test both the cases where a behavior should occur and where it shouldn't. One-sided evals create one-sided optimization." "It's often better to grade what the agent produced, not the path it took" — avoid checking specific tool-call sequences so creative-but-valid approaches aren't punished.
facts.limits: General guidance for agent evals, not a statement about `claude plugin eval`'s own defaults, though it aligns with observed defaults (runs default 3 maps to a small-k regime; the file_exists/outcome-grading style maps to "grade what was produced").

facts.feature: skill-creator blog: comparator/benchmark tooling (a separate tool from `claude plugin eval`)
facts.behavior: Describes comparator agents for blind A/B testing ("two skill versions, or skill vs. no skill. They judge outputs without knowing which is which"), a "benchmark mode" tracking "eval pass rate, elapsed time, and token usage" after model updates, regression detection ("Running evals against a new model gives you an early signal"), and multi-agent parallel eval runs ("each in a clean context with its own token and timing metrics. Faster results, no cross-contamination").
facts.limits: This describes the skill-creator plugin's own bundled eval scripts (run_eval.py / run_loop.py / aggregate_benchmark.py per this repo's own secondary survey, docs/handbook/sources/testing-sweep.md), which is a distinct tool bundled inside one specific official plugin — not the general-purpose `claude plugin eval` CLI command documented elsewhere in this report. The blog post itself does not name `claude plugin eval`.

facts.behavior: A repo secondary source attributes to "the built-in runner's own guidance" the line: "Prefer deterministic graders for long artifacts; llm judges are noisy on long inputs."
facts.limits: This exact quote was not independently located in `claude plugin eval --help`, `claude plugin eval init --help`, or either of the two fetched Anthropic docs pages — it may originate from the gated interactive `init` interview flow (which requires an interactive terminal this session did not have) or from case/grader authoring guidance not reachable here. Reported as unverified secondary-source content, not confirmed primary-source text.
facts.citation: docs/handbook/testing.md (quoting an unverified source; not independently located in the CLI help or fetched docs pages)
